title: Audit log displays user full name instead of user ID
gherkin:
Given a user with ID '12345' and full name 'John Smith' performs an action
When the action is recorded in the audit log
Then the audit log entry should display 'John Smith' as the user identity
And the audit log entry should not display only the numeric user ID '12345'
rationale: Human-readable audit identity requires that user names be displayed in audit logs rather than system-generated numeric identifiers, making it easier for auditors to understand who performed an action.

generationSummary: Test cases for human-readable audit identity requirement. These tests verify that audit logs contain identifiable information about users and entities in a format that is easily understood by humans, rather than system identifiers or cryptic codes.

title: Audit log displays entity name in human-readable format

rationale: Audit logs should identify entities (databases, systems, resources) using their human-readable names to make audit trails understandable to non-technical auditors.

rationale: Human-readable audit identity explicitly requires avoiding cryptic or system-generated codes that would be difficult for humans to interpret without additional lookup tools.

rationale: Human-readable audit identity must persist even when the original user or entity is deleted, requiring fallback mechanisms to maintain audit trail readability.

title: Audit log identity is consistent across all audit entries

Given a user 'Alice Johnson' performs multiple actions over time

rationale: Consistent human-readable identities across audit logs make it easier to track actions by the same user and ensure audit trail integrity and readability.
